title: Looking for few people to try breaking my text RPG engine (new release today!)
author: legend-of-alan
selftext:
Hey all, I've been building something I thought turn-based RPG fans might enjoy.

It's called Spookery. It's an open-source Rust engine for persistent worlds, and it runs a bit like a private server.

At runtime, the optional AI game master (can be a human or none, too) plugs in with your API key, adds some extra flavor, and makes moves for NPCs, but it can only propose moves. The engine owns the state and checks every move deterministically against the rules before anything changes. The idea is to reduce hallucinations and token burn. It stops the AI hallucinating dice rolls, there's no expensive setup of AI auditors checking AI output, and I'm tinkering with agent tech to cut calls. Devs build worlds, moves, items, cast members, etc. in agent-editable YAML.

A new release is out today and I'd love it if a few people could give 10 or 15 minutes to test it. Here's what I'm looking for:

1. Play the demo for a bit. You can do this with or without the AI GM. Without it, NPCs still do their programmed reactions (like counter-rolling dice), but they won't decide to make moves on their own.
2. Open your coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, whatever you use) and change the demo with the pack-author skill. Add a room, an NPC, a new rule, etc.
3. Play it again and see if your change actually works.

Mostly I want to find where you get stuck. Confusing docs, the agent fighting the skill, build problems, anything you wish was smoother. Rough notes are totally fine.

**It's still early days, so a few things to know:** The terminal client is ugly, I know, and networking is off (everything is localhost). But the backend and the agent side are coming along nicely.

It's also really modular. In the future anyone could plug the engine into whatever server runtime they want, build a client on whatever frontend they like, and even reuse the AI agent in a custom client.

Links: [Repo on GitHub](https://github.com/legend-of-alan/spookery) and [Latest Releases](https://github.com/legend-of-alan/spookery/releases)

Comment here or open an issue on GitHub (I'm also active on Substack). Cheers!
